dimensions.projectionState: Exactly one of the ten states below; stale and error cannot be relabeled fresh.

states.meaning: no current usable record; one foreground request may be in flight
current generation and wall-clock freshness window agree
stale-but-admissible payload visible while one background refresh runs
transient refresh failure retained an explicit stale fallback
current saved identity and an admissible stale snapshot are available offline
hard age or clock safety rule forbids projection; refetch required
refresh failed without an admissible payload or security/integrity error suppresses it
identity or generation changed; prior result is no longer projectable
mutation acknowledgement installed a newer durable fence and invalidated prior values
payload is corrupt, partial, unsupported, or bound to another identity/key

ttlBoundaryRules.rule: stale iff softTtlMs <= nowWallMs - lastValidatedAtWallMs < hardMaxAgeSincePayloadFetch
wall clock moved backward or timestamps are inverted => CLOCK_ANOMALY; never fresh
large forward wall-clock jump may only move toward stale or expired, never fresher
monotonic elapsedRealtime controls in-process timeout, cooldown and single-flight deadlines; it never proves persisted age across reboot
response latency is not an age source and cannot extend freshness
a valid current-fence 304 renews lastValidatedAtWallMs and soft freshness only; default policy does not renew hard age since payload fetch
stale-if-error requires current identity/fence, previously complete payload, transient error class and an unexpired policy window
offline stale uses the same wall-clock and hard-age checks as online stale; unknown identity remains fail-closed

preconditions: current identity and generation fence before request and before commit
stored complete payload and stored validator
conditional request actually sent with that validator
304 response class is explicitly supported by the active transport adapter
acceptedEffect: payload body remains byte-equivalent and untouched
lastValidatedAtWallMs is set from a trusted local clock after response
soft freshness restarts only if hard payload age remains valid
single-flight owner completes only under the same generation
conditional304.s3Boundary: G1-S3 records zero OpenAPI 304 responses and zero ETag response headers. This contract does not claim Jellyfin endpoint support and is dormant unless a runtime adapter can prove a valid conditional exchange.

blockedErrorClasses: clock anomaly outside an explicitly approved grace policy
staleIfError.projectionRule: Allowed fallback is visible only with stale=true, reason, savedAt and lastAttemptAt. A blocked class suppresses old payload.

clock.processAuthority: monotonic clock for request timeouts, cooldowns and in-flight deadlines
clock.backwardStep: CLOCK_ANOMALY; no fresh claim; refetch or explicit stale fallback only if policy permits
clock.forwardStep: recompute conservatively; hard max age may immediately expire

trigger: authoritative server event for the same identity and affected resource
atomicObligation: increment durable namespace generation before any old snapshot can be projected
persist affected key prefixes or namespace tombstone/watermark
cancel or detach in-flight old-generation owners
reject every commit whose captured generation differs
mutationInvalidation.writeAfterInvariant: For every pre-mutation record, freshClaimAllowed=false after the mutation commit is durable.
mutationInvalidation.localIntentBoundary: client-only accepted intent is not authoritative success and must not fabricate a cache refresh

requiredPolicy: hard behavior when pinned records exceed cap
capacity.admission: Reserve quota before write; a degraded write cannot publish partial bytes.
capacity.overCap: Evict only eligible unpinned records or reject/degrade the new write; never silently exceed a hard cap.

mustHave: never evict another account as a substitute
never evict a payload with an active mutation obligation

requirements: pin has owner, generation and deadline
pin count and bytes are bounded
expired/orphan pins are recovered after process death

inFlightDedupe.key: principalContext + serverId + userId + logicalKeyDigest + generationFence + fetchMode
inFlightDedupe.joinerRule: A joiner may reuse only the exact current-fence operation and must not receive another identity's result.
inFlightDedupe.ownerRule: One owner commits; late completion after fence change is discarded.
inFlightDedupe.failureRule: Owner failure may be retried by one current-fence owner; stale joiners are cancelled.

singleWriter.logicalRule: At most one committed writer per namespace/key generation.
singleWriter.inProcessMinimum: Serialize commit and generation check in one critical section.
singleWriter.crossProcessMinimum: Use a durable compare-and-increment/CAS fence and atomic file/DB publication; an in-memory HashMap lock is insufficient.

crossProcess.mandatoryInvariant: No older generation may commit, become fresh, or project after a newer fence is durable.
requiredFixtures: two writers same key, one generation advances
writer A delayed after account switch to B
mutation in process A followed by lookup in process B
crash between payload write and fence/tombstone publication

corruption.action: do not project; quarantine/delete only the validated target; issue a bounded refetch
corruption.mustNot: repair by borrowing another account, another page, or stale bytes from an unverified file

decisionPoints: production soft TTL and hard max age
eviction order, pin cap and prefetch cap
whether any runtime 304 adapter is supported
